A Russian cargo ship is on fire in the eastern Gulf of Finland. The Finnish Border Guard is leading the maritime rescue operation and is preparing for potential environmental damage control within Finland's area of responsibility.
The damaged vessel has currently drifted from international waters into Finnish territorial waters in the Eastern Gulf of Finland. The situation poses no danger to other maritime traffic.
Border Guard will provide further updates as operations progress. Preparations for potential rescue operations are being coordinated with other authorities, both domestically and internationally.
Border Guard is responsible for maritime rescue and oil spill response within Finland's area of responsibility.

sources.text: Defense Drones strike Russian military-linked cargo ship in Gulf of Finland ByGabriele Petrauskaite November 22, 2026, 11:08 GMT+02:00 3 minute read f x in Russian military-linked cargo ship A Russian cargo ship linked to the country’s military logistics network caught fire after a drone attack in the Gulf of Finland on November 21, 2026. The damaged vessel drifted into Finnish territorial waters, where authorities coordinated a rescue and firefighting operation involving Finnish, Estonian and Russian units. The ship, Sparta II, was sailing from St. Petersburg toward Russia’s Kaliningrad exclave when it was hit. Finnish military officials said Ukraine was likely behind the attack, although Kyiv had not publicly claimed responsibility. Drone attack damages ship Finnish Defence Forces detected a drone attack against the Russian cargo vessel on November 21, 2026, west of Gogland Island in the eastern Gulf of Finland. Estonia’s Police and Border Guard Board said the explosions occurred while the ship was in Estonia’s exclusive economic zone, outside its territorial waters, in an international shipping lane. Finnish authorities initially described the attack location as international waters. Russian officials said two drones struck the vessel. Finnish authorities confirmed a drone attack but did not independently confirm the number of drones involved. The strike damaged the ship and started a fire. The vessel subsequently lost its ability to maneuver and drifted north into Finnish waters, eventually anchoring off the coastal town of Loviisa. The Sparta II is a Russian-flagged cargo ship associated with Oboronlogistika, a company that provides logistics services to Russia’s Ministry of Defence. The vessel is under US and Ukrainian sanctions and has previously been linked to the transport of Russian military equipment. Finnish authorities said they did not know what cargo was aboard during the incident. They did not confirm that the ship was carrying weapons or military supplies at the time of the attack. Crew evacuated as fire continues The ship’s 16 crew members were evacuated on the evening of November 21, 2026. They left the vessel in lifeboats and life rafts before being transferred to a nearby Russian cargo ship. Finnish Border Guard units led the maritime rescue operation. Finnish patrol vessels, aircraft and helicopters were deployed, alongside rescue tugs and an Estonian patrol vessel. A Russian rescue ship, Murman, also joined the operation at the request of Finnish authorities. The Sparta II remained anchored off Loviisa on November 22. Firefighting and cooling operations continued aboard the vessel. Finnish officials said the fire was no longer spreading, although it had not been fully extinguished. Authorities prepared to tow the damaged ship into Russia’s maritime area of responsibility. The operation was also intended to reduce the risk of environmental damage in the Gulf of Finland. Finland introduces air and maritime traffic restrictions Finland temporarily restricted air and maritime traffic in the eastern Gulf of Finland twice on November 21. The measures were introduced as a precaution amid reports of drone activity and to allow authorities to respond safely to potential threats. The restrictions were later lifted. Finnish Prime Minister Petteri Orpo said the incident showed how Russia’s war against Ukraine was affecting the country’s neighboring regions. Orpo also stated that Ukraine had the right to defend itself against Russia’s invasion. Hours after the ship was struck, Finland reported a suspected violation of its airspace by a Russian helicopter near Loviisa. Finnish Defence Minister Antti Hakkanen said the helicopter may have been involved in rescue or monitoring operations connected to the damaged vessel. The Finnish Border Guard is investigating the suspected airspace violation. Drones increasingly threaten Russian logistics in the Baltic The attack took place amid Ukraine’s continued use of long-range drones against Russian military and infrastructure targets far from the front line. Russia’s Leningrad region, which includes major Baltic ports and logistics facilities, has faced repeated drone attacks. The Gulf of Finland is an important shipping route for Russian ports such as St. Petersburg and Ust-Luga. The Sparta II incident highlights the risks for vessels linked to Russian military logistics operating in the Baltic Sea. It also raises concerns for neighboring countries, as damaged ships, drifting vessels and potential drone incursions can require emergency responses beyond the immediate area of an attack. The drone strike has not been publicly claimed by Ukraine. The exact type of drones used, their launch point and the ship’s cargo have not been confirmed yet. drone Finland Russia Leave a Reply Cancel reply Your email address will not be published. sources.text: Swipe for next article Russian ship burns off Finland after suspected drone attack: ‘War is spilling over’ Finland and Sweden are NATO's newest member states Rich Booth Sunday 22 November 2026 09:28 GMT Bookmark Comments Go to comments Bookmark popover Removed from bookmarks Close popover Russian military vehicles spotted near Finland border Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Join today Already a member? Log in A cargo ship with Russian military connections was still burning late on Saturday as it sat at anchor in Finnish waters, with Finland leading the rescue operation after what it said was likely a Ukrainian attack. Finnish authorities said Russian vessels might eventually tow the wreckage back to Russia. The 16-member crew of the Sparta II abandoned the vessel for lifeboats before transferring to a nearby Russian ship, and is now heading back to Russia, Finnish Border Guard Commander Ilja Iljin told public broadcaster Yle late on Saturday. The ship was struck by drones and caught fire in the Baltic Sea on Saturday, in an incident Finland said was likely an attack by Ukraine, and it later drifted into Finnish waters. Finland's Defence Forces said the vessel, which was bound for the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad, was damaged in international waters west of Russia's Gogland island, corroborating an earlier account from Russian officials. open image in gallery The Russian cargo ship Sparta II during fire extinguishing at a location given as the Gulf of Finland, November 21, 2026. (Reuters) Ukraine has sent waves of military drones towards Russia's northwest Leningrad region this year, including some that strayed into the airspace of the Baltic region, leading to fears that the war was affecting NATO territory. "It is likely that Ukraine... is behind (the attack)," Finnish armed forces spokesperson Aki-Mauri Huhtinen told a press conference, adding it was not clear why the ⁠vessel had been targeted. Mikko Simola, commander of the Gulf of Finland Coast Guard, said a Russian helicopter was suspected of briefly violating Finnish airspace during the rescue operation. 'WAR IS ​SPILLING OVER' Helsinki said it had introduced temporary aviation and maritime restrictions in the ‌eastern Gulf of Finland to protect civilians and allow authorities to operate if drones needed to be intercepted. "The war is spilling over into our neighbouring areas. Finnish authorities are handling the situation in the Gulf of Finland, where a drone strike has hit a Russian merchant vessel. Ukraine has the right to fight ‌against the aggressor," Finnish Prime Minister Petteri Orpo said on X. Sweden's Defence Minister Pal Jonson said Swedish combat aircraft, operating under ‌Finnish command, took part in safeguarding Finland's and NATO's territorial integrity following the incident. Finland and Sweden are NATO's newest member states, joining the military alliance in 2023 and 2024, respectively, in response to Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. "The consequences of fighting Russia's aggression have reached the Baltic Sea. Another signal for the aggressor to stop. But nothing will stop us from supporting ⁠Ukraine," Estonia's Prime Minister Kristen Michal wrote on X. Estonia's government said it had sent a navy vessel to assist in the rescue operation, including firefighting and pollution response. Ukraine's Foreign Ministry did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Russia's embassy in Helsinki did not immediately respond to requests for comment. The vessel is subject to US sanctions and is linked to Russian shipping company Oboronlogistika, according to the US Treasury Department. According to the company's website, Oboronlogistika provides logistics services for the Russian Defence Ministry. "At the moment, there is no confirmed information about what cargo is on board, but it cannot be ruled out that there is military materiel on board," Iljin of the Finnish Border Guard said. Leningrad region Governor Aleksandr Drozdenko said on Telegram that a cargo vessel had been attacked ‌by two drones in international waters about 3 nautical miles from Russia's border. open image in gallery The damaged Russian cargo ship Sparta II, in a location given as the Gulf of Finland (Reuters) Drozdenko also said 80 drones had been shot down over the Leningrad ​region overnight. Finland's military said last week it had detected a strike on a Russian warship in the same area during a wave ‌of Ukrainian drone attacks on the Leningrad region. Kaliningrad Governor Alexei Besprozvannykh said ⁠the incident posed no threat to supplies to the region. Kaliningrad, which lies between Poland and Lithuania, has periodically been a flashpoint between Russia and ⁤NATO and the European Union. Russia has previously described attacks on its commercial vessels outside its territorial waters as acts of terrorism and maritime piracy. The Sparta II is a 121-metre (397-foot) Russian-flagged cargo vessel owned by Oboronlogistika ‌that left St Petersburg on Friday, according to LSEG ​data. The Gulf of Finland is a narrow arm of the Baltic Sea between ‌Finland and Estonia that extends east to St Petersburg. Gogland lies in ​the eastern Gulf of Finland. paragraphs.text: Venäläinen rahtialus Sparta II syttyi palamaan lauantaina 21. marraskuuta itäisellä Suomenlahdella, kun siihen tehtiin drooni-isku. Puolustusvoimien mukaan alus vaurioitui kansainvälisillä vesillä Suursaaren länsipuolella. Sen jälkeen se ajautui Suomen aluevesille.
Suomen puolustusvoimien mukaan iskun takana on todennäköisesti Ukraina.
Aluksen 16 miehistön jäsentä jättivät aluksen pelastusveneillä ja siirtyivät lähellä olleeseen venäläiseen alukseen.

Independentin mukaan rajavartiolaitoksen Ilja Iljin kertoi lauantai-iltana Ylelle, että miehistö on matkalla takaisin Venäjälle. Lehden mukaan alus paloi yhä myöhään lauantaina ankkurissa Suomen vesillä, ja Suomen viranomaisten mukaan venäläiset alukset saattavat lopulta hinata sen Venäjälle.

Aerotimen mukaan alus oli sunnuntaina ankkurissa Loviisan edustalla. Suomen viranomaisten mukaan palo ei enää levinnyt, mutta sitä ei ollut saatu kokonaan sammutettua. Viranomaiset valmistautuivat hinaamaan aluksen Venäjän vastuulla olevalle merialueelle, osin ympäristövahinkojen riskin pienentämiseksi.

Rajavartiolaitos kertoi lauantaina, että se johtaa meripelastusta ja valmistautuu torjumaan mahdollisia ympäristövahinkoja Suomen vastuualueella. Sen mukaan tilanne ei vaaranna muuta meriliikennettä. Valmisteluja sovitetaan yhteen muiden viranomaisten kanssa Suomessa ja ulkomailla.

Aerotimen mukaan pelastukseen osallistui suomalaisia partioaluksia, lentokoneita, helikoptereita ja pelastushinaajia sekä virolainen partioalus. Myös venäläinen pelastusalus Murman tuli mukaan Suomen viranomaisten pyynnöstä.

Independentin mukaan Viron hallitus lähetti avuksi laivaston aluksen sammutus- ja ympäristövahinkojen torjuntatöihin. Ruotsin puolustusministeri Pål Jonson kertoi ruotsalaisten hävittäjien osallistuneen Suomen johdolla Suomen ja Naton alueellisen koskemattomuuden turvaamiseen.

Sparta II on Venäjän lipun alla purjehtiva rahtialus, joka oli matkalla Pietarista Kaliningradiin. Se liittyy yhtiöön nimeltä Oboronlogistika, joka tarjoaa logistiikkapalveluja Venäjän puolustusministeriölle, ja on Yhdysvaltojen pakotteiden kohteena. Suomen viranomaiset eivät tiedä, mitä aluksessa oli lastina.
Independentin mukaan Iljin sanoi, ettei sotatarvikkeiden olemassaoloa aluksessa voi sulkea pois. Lehden mukaan alus on 121 metriä pitkä.

Iskupaikasta on eri tietoja. Aerotimen mukaan Viron poliisi- ja rajavartiolaitos kertoi räjähdysten tapahtuneen Viron talousvyöhykkeellä, aluevesien ulkopuolella. Venäjän viranomaisten mukaan alukseen osui kaksi droonia, mutta Suomen viranomaiset eivät ole vahvistaneet määrää. Ukraina ei ole ottanut iskua julkisesti nimiinsä.

Independentin mukaan Leningradin alueen kuvernööri Aleksandr Drozdenko kertoi kahden droonin iskeneen alukseen kansainvälisillä vesillä noin kolmen meripeninkulman päässä Venäjän rajasta. Lehden mukaan Suomen puolustusvoimat havaitsi jo edellisellä viikolla iskun venäläiseen sota-alukseen samalla alueella.
Suomi rajoitti lauantaina tilapäisesti lento- ja meriliikennettä itäisellä Suomenlahdella, jotta viranomaiset voisivat toimia turvallisesti droonien varalta.
Aerotimen mukaan rajoitukset otettiin käyttöön kahdesti ja ne on sittemmin purettu.
Venäläisen helikopterin epäillään loukanneen Suomen ilmatilaa pelastusoperaation aikana.

Aerotimen mukaan epäilty loukkaus tapahtui Loviisan lähellä. Puolustusministeri Antti Häkkäsen mukaan helikopteri on voinut liittyä aluksen pelastukseen tai tarkkailuun. Rajavartiolaitos tutkii tapausta.
Pääministeri Petteri Orpo sanoi sodan ulottuvan Suomen lähialueille ja totesi, että Ukrainalla on oikeus puolustautua hyökkääjää vastaan.

reasons: Otsikko 'Venäläinen rahtialus ajautui palavana Suomen aluevesille' on 56 merkkiä, ja tärkein asia on alussa. Lähde A/B (Rajavartiolaitoksen tiedote 21.11.: alus palaa ja on ajautunut kansainvälisiltä vesiltä Suomen aluevesille) ja lähde C tukevat sitä.

Ingressi on tuettu. Drooni-isku ja palo lauantaina 21.11. tulevat lähteistä C ja D, ja 21.11.2026 on lauantai.
